manage.lead: Harmless: treat only if they bother the patient.

points: Neonatal milia resolve within weeks; many adult milia persist but are harmless.
De-roof with a sterile needle or blade and express the keratin (trained clinician).
Topical retinoid; treat the underlying blistering disease; avoid potent topical steroids on the face.

items.t: Milia with skin fragility, blisters and scarring on the backs of the hands: investigate for **porphyria cutanea tarda** or epidermolysis bullosa.
Milia en plaque or widespread milia: dermatology.

quiz.a: Tiny superficial keratin cysts (miniature epidermoid cysts), 1–2 mm, white.

quiz.q: Name three causes of secondary milia.
quiz.a: Blistering diseases (PCT, EB, pemphigoid), burns or dermabrasion, potent topical steroids.
De-roofing with a sterile needle or blade and gentle expression.
No; they resolve on their own within weeks.
